title: Assassination of Chris Hani
summary: On 10 April 1993 Chris Hani, leader of the South African Communist Party, was shot dead outside his home in Boksburg by Janusz Walus, a Polish immigrant, in a plot with Conservative Party MP Clive Derby-Lewis. The killing threatened to derail the negotiations ending apartheid; both men were convicted and later refused amnesty.

as_recorded.value: On April 10, the day of the murder (page dated to the 1997 hearing; the killing is placed in April 1993)

where.modern_name: Boksburg, Gauteng, South Africa (pin at the town centre; the shooting was outside Hani's home)
where.historical_name: Boksburg, East Rand, Republic of South Africa

importance.justification: Political assassination of a leading ANC-aligned figure during the 1990s transition, widely seen as a test of the negotiations.

audience_note: Describes a political assassination; the victim's teenage daughter was present.

sources.title: Chris Hani: the men behind his killing
